answer: Proposal: an account registers a hardware-enclave key, sealed so software cannot mirror it; the manufacturer attests one key per physical die — issuer honesty is the stated trust. On-ledger a chip key is a vertex registered once, ever; reuse is rejected, so each extra identity permanently consumes one chip. The protocol caps the reward river per vertex below a registered chip's depreciation — resale recovers most of a phone's price — so N heads cost N×depreciation and earn ≤ N×cap. Honest users pay zero marginal cost. Seams: bulk-issued keys, TEE exploits.
